explanation: A receiver times signals from at least four satellites. Their clocks are so precise that Einstein's relativity must be allowed for, or positions would drift by about 10 km a day.

claims.text: GPS receivers work out their position from radio signals sent by satellites.
GPS itself works from satellite signals, not from phone masts, Earth's magnetic field or radar echoes.
A GPS receiver needs signals from at least four satellites to fix its position in three dimensions and correct its own clock.
Without corrections for relativity, GPS positions would drift by about 10 km a day.
